title: Credential split across lines by a string-literal line continuation
summary: A SendGrid-shaped key inside a Python or JavaScript string literal is broken by a backslash at a line end, so the literal continues on the next line.
rationale: In both languages the backslash-newline inside a string literal contributes nothing to the string value, so the program holds the intact key while the file holds two fragments and a separator. A reader that treats the line break as content, or that covers only one line, misses the credential; a reader that applied the same rule outside a string literal would be wrong.

expectation.rationale: Flagged, with every fragment covered. The Python reference (Python Software Foundation) and the ECMAScript specification (Ecma) are both consistent with the reading that a backslash-newline in a string literal is ignored. Stated as consistency of two texts, not as a provider rule. Synthetic, never issued: every value in the fixtures is built from the words SYNTHETIC and EXAMPLE, so none can authenticate.

sources.supports: A backslash at the end of a line inside a string literal ignores the newline; neither is part of the string value.
A LineContinuation in a string literal has the empty String as its string value; a line terminator can appear in a string literal only as part of a LineContinuation.
sources.locator: 12.9.4 String Literals, Static Semantics: SV and Note
